Control study · Transaction perimeter → memory perimeter

Sell the Company, Keep the Archive?

A company sale and an archive transfer can be designed as separate but coordinated transactions; what may or should be separated depends on ownership, contracts, duties, taxes, privacy, culture, and jurisdiction.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

“The company was sold” hides the asset perimeter. Equity, trademarks, designs, copyrights, domains, inventory, contracts, customer data, samples, records, personal papers, artworks, and physical garments may not share one owner or transfer mechanism. U.S. trademark and copyright statutes provide particular assignment and transfer rules; public SEC agreements demonstrate negotiated allocations, not universal outcomes.

An archive is also not a neutral box of old things. It may contain employee and collaborator records, confidential business information, personal data, culturally sensitive knowledge, licensed images, physical objects owned by others, and evidence needed for continuing obligations. Separating an archive can protect research independence or founder memory; it can also strand the operating company, violate agreements, obscure accountability, or create two incomplete histories.

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · PERIMETER

What exactly is in the deal?

Inventory entity interests and each asset class with current owner, custodian, governing record, restriction, liability, and desired treatment. Do not infer asset ownership from brand presentation.

PROPOSALS35S36

02 · TRANSFER

What mechanism moves each asset?

Distinguish equity sale, asset sale, trademark assignment, copyright transfer, license, loan, deposit, donation, data transfer, and services or transition arrangement.

VERIFIEDS49S55S63

03 · ARCHIVE

What must remain connected?

Map originals and copies, provenance, restrictions, operational dependencies, privacy, legal hold, contributor access, research terms, correction, and future interpretation.

INFERENCES08S39S65

04 · AFTER

Who can use and explain the history?

Define access, digitization, exhibition, licensing, publication, brand reference, authentication, enforcement cooperation, funding, custody, and dispute mechanisms.

PROPOSALS40S42

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

A founder-retained archive may preserve dissenting memory or become a private leverage device. A buyer-held archive may support continuity or rewrite history. Neither custody choice guarantees ethical stewardship.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Build an asset-by-asset transaction and archive inventory.
  2. Attach title, assignment, license, consent, privacy, and custody evidence.
  3. Run operational, research, worker, collaborator, customer, and public-interest consequences.
  4. Take the actual deal structure to transaction, IP, privacy, tax, employment, and archive specialists.

Reading protocol

Every material statement carries an evidence label and point-of-claim source links. Interpretation is never presented as source fact. Legal sections identify their jurisdiction; state, foreign, contractual, beneficial-ownership, validity, priority, and disputed-fact questions remain counsel-review gates. This exhibition is educational and does not provide legal, conservation, or business advice.
